children: Javed Farooqui Mumbai: The suspension of Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC) ratings has created an opening for cable and DTH operators to establish an alternative source of television viewership data under the ministry of information and broadcasting's TV ratings policy. GTPL Hathway has made an early move by publishing data from its return-path-data (RPD)-based service, but the larger question is whether operator-led measurement can emerge as a credible industry-wide alternative.

Its viability will depend on the scale and representativeness of the data, sampling methodology and the ability to establish credibility among broadcasters and advertisers, industry sources said. RPD captures viewing information from connected set-top boxes (STBs), tracking which channels households watch and for how long. Unlike BARC's panel-based system, which uses people meters and household-member information to estimate individual viewing, RPD typically records viewing at the household or device level.

Its industry-wide relevance will depend on scale, geographical representation and methodological transparency. GTPL is tracking viewing through 10,000 STBs and plans to expand to 50,000, working with TAM India to generate the data. Tata Play has also used RPD for years, primarily for internal content planning, according to industry sources. BARC earlier piloted RPD with Airtel Digital TV and DEN Networks, but the initiative failed to scale as operators sought compensation for sharing data and costs proved prohibitive.

title: BARC Ratings Ban: GTPL Hathway Uses RPD Model to Publish Own Data
